title: Plano Carpini's Mission to the Mongols
summary: Pope Innocent IV sent the Franciscans John of Plano Carpini and Benedict the Pole to the Mongol khan. Leaving Lyons in April 1245, they crossed Batu's lands and reached the imperial camp near Karakorum in July 1246, where Güyük was being chosen Great Khan. Carpini returned in 1247 and wrote an account.

uncertainty.note: Journey 1245-1247; arrival at Güyük's camp on 22 July 1246 per Carpini's text as translated; Güyük's formal seating came weeks later and its exact date was not confirmed here, so the 'July 1246 enthronement' lead is not asserted.

as_recorded.calendar: Julian-style feast-day dating in translated text

where.historical_name: Güyük's imperial camp (Sira Orda) near Karakorum, Mongol Empire

importance.justification: One of the first European papal embassies to the Mongol court, producing an eyewitness report of the khan's election.

sources.title: The Journey of Friar John of Pian de Carpine to the Court of Kuyuk Khan, 1245-1247
sources.author: W. W. Rockhill (translation)

sources.title: The Franciscan Friar who went to the Mongol Empire

reviewer_note: Pin is a proxy: UNESCO's Orkhon-Kharkorin property reference point (N47 28 45.17 E102 40 42.535), not the camp itself, which the sources place only 'near Karakorum'. Güyük's enthronement date not confirmed; I did not read the whole UW text.
